<Picture 1> is the exact A0 empty-stage opening frame. <Picture 2> is the exact A1 completed Chinese soy-milk-and-youtiao closing frame.

STRICT AUDIO OUTPUT POLICY:
Generate diegetic Foley sound effects only. The audio track may contain only short, dry, non-tonal sounds caused by visible physical actions. Every audible event must begin and end with its corresponding visible movement. Leave near-digital silence between actions. Do not generate a continuous ambience layer.

Absolutely no background music, score, soundtrack, melody, harmony, chords, bass line, beat, arranged rhythm, percussion pattern, drum sound, tonal drone, ambient pad, sustained musical tone, orchestral layer, electronic texture, jingle, intro music, outro music, transition sting, riser, cinematic boom, musical whoosh, emotional underscore, singing, humming, choir, or vocalization. Do not infer music from the Chinese setting, breakfast theme, morning atmosphere, theater design, or stop-motion style.

0.0–0.6 seconds:
Hold the exact state of <Picture 1>. The theater box, five arched openings, overhead lamps, dark-green curtains, wooden floor, central circular turntable, and two foreground rails remain still.

0.6–2.2 seconds:
Five separate Chinese environment acrylic standees enter. The teal-green tiled roof eave and wooden lattice breakfast-shop window slide independently from the left. The black iron wok rises through its floor slot. The bamboo steamer stack and gray-brick alley doorway slide independently from the right. Every standee retains visible thickness, a clear acrylic perimeter, and its own support foot. Each piece decelerates, makes one small rebound, and locks with a wooden click.

2.2–3.2 seconds:
The ceramic soy-milk pot enters on the left midground rail while the stack of breakfast bowls enters on the right midground rail. Both decelerate, rebound slightly, and lock without blocking the turntable.

3.2–4.0 seconds:
The woven bamboo draining basket slides in on the left foreground rail. The blue-and-white porcelain spoon slides in on the right foreground rail.

4.0–5.1 seconds:
A breakfast carrier holding an upright blue-and-white porcelain bowl of soy milk and an empty white shallow plate moves onto the central turntable along a physical center rail. It shows believable weight and inertia, makes one small forward-and-back rebound, and locks. The soy milk remains level and does not spill.

5.1–5.9 seconds:
One temporary bamboo tong descends on a thin suspension line, holding exactly two complete parallel golden youtiao. It gently places both youtiao onto the white plate. The youtiao make physical contact and perform one small settling bounce. The tong releases them and fully retracts upward. It must not remain in the closing frame. The youtiao must not bend, duplicate, split, melt, or break.

5.7–6.3 seconds:
Exactly two rigid steam-shaped acrylic standees descend on visible suspension lines. One stops above the soy-milk bowl and one above the background wok. They retain clear edges and physical thickness and never behave like volumetric smoke.

6.3–7.0 seconds:
All motion ends. Mechanical vibration decays rapidly into near-digital silence. Hold the exact state of <Picture 2> without beginning another action.

Maintain the locked camera and permanent theater geometry throughout. No zoom, pan, tilt, orbit, reframing, or cut. No fade, dissolve, crossfade, digital transition, magical transformation, in-place replacement, spontaneous appearance, unsupported floating, or visual drift. Generate no people, subtitles, readable text, letters, numerals, place names, flags, logos, watermarks, or text containers.

AUDIO-VISUAL CAUSALITY LOCK:
Generate a sound only when its visible physical source is moving or making contact. Stop the sound immediately when the action stops. All Foley must be dry, close-miked, brief, low in reverberation, and irregular rather than rhythmic. Do not fill quiet intervals. The final portion must remain near-silent after the last mechanical vibration settles.
